title: Implicit Neural Representations of Individual Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2606.12200v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study policy representation learning from unlabeled multi-policy behavioral data. Each episode is generated by a fixed policy, but policy labels are unavailable. This setting appears in robotics play, demonstrations, games, racing, and other datasets where heterogeneous behaviors are mixed without annotations. We introduce Behavioral INR, a self-supervised generative model that adapts implicit neural representations (INRs) from vision to behavior. Instead of mapping coordinates to RGB values, Behavioral INR represents a policy as a state-action function mapping states to subsequent actions. An episode-level latent modulates this function through FiLM layers, yielding a generative prior over policies and allowing policy identity to be inferred without supervision. translated_title: 个体行为的隐式神经表示
translated_abstract: 我们研究从无标签的多策略行为数据中进行策略表示学习。每个轨迹片段由一个固定策略生成，但策略标签不可用。这种场景出现在机器人自由玩耍、演示、游戏、赛车以及其他异构行为混合且无标注的数据集中。我们提出了Behavioral INR，一种将视觉领域中的隐式神经表示（INR）适配到行为领域的自监督生成模型。Behavioral INR不是将坐标映射到RGB值，而是将策略表示为一个状态-动作函数，即把状态映射到后续动作。一个片段级的潜在变量通过FiLM层对该函数进行调制，从而产生策略之上的生成先验，并允许在无监督条件下推断策略身份。由于INR将每个数据点视为来自某个底层函数的样本，同一模型能够自然地适应不同的片段长度和不同的采样粒度……
tldr: 提出Behavioral INR，一种自监督生成模型，将视觉领域的隐式神经表示适配到行为领域，把策略表示为由片段级潜在变量通过FiLM层调制的状态-动作函数，从而在无标签的混合行为数据中实现无监督的策略表示学习与策略身份推断。
en_tdlr: Behavioral INR adapts implicit neural representations from vision to behavior, representing policies as state-action functions modulated by episode-level latents via FiLM layers, enabling self-supervised policy representation learning and identity inference from unlabeled multi-policy behavioral data.
